states.label: Recorded two-space cave

phase.label: Published survey arrangement; ancient architectural date unknown

states.note: Sion records two spaces and two mouths in the eastern cliff. Observation belongs to the published survey, not a current field visit.

states.label: Recorded northern aperture

phase.label: Published survey arrangement; ancient architectural date unknown

states.note: Corrected repeat identity: right/clear opening is northern after reading the published north arrow. Aperture chord is a 2D proxy; threshold height and ancient phase unknown.

states.label: Recorded southern remaining gap

phase.label: Published survey arrangement; ancient architectural date unknown

states.note: Left/built-wall opening is southern. The surviving gap cannot recover the full pre-wall aperture.

states.label: Recorded rock-cut pillar

phase.label: Published survey arrangement; ancient architectural date unknown

states.note: Separates the reported spaces. No reviewed endpoint set or dated cutting contact defines a pillar outline.

states.label: Recorded partial mouth-blocking wall

phase.label: Published survey arrangement; ancient architectural date unknown

states.note: Published length 2.4 m, thickness about 0.4 m. No sealed construction date or traced plan polygon is supplied.

states.label: Published Hellenistic-use reconstruction

phase.label: First half of second century to first half of first century BCE
phase.dating_basis: Excavator use reconstruction from cave finds

states.note: This use interpretation and conflict/concealment explanation do not independently date the wall, pillar or threshold.

states.label: Ancient southern aperture before blocking

phase.label: Pre-wall arrangement, date unknown

states.note: An original wider mouth is a proposed configuration. Its boundary, date and accessible width are unestablished.

states.label: Ancient northern threshold required by the depth branch

phase.label: Instruction-period threshold, date unknown

states.note: No ancient threshold level or phase-controlled surface is recorded. z_target = z_threshold − depth remains symbolic.

depth_branch.interpretation: Exploratory vertical branch; not entrance width

states.label: D9 Middle Bronze shaft

phase.label: Middle Bronze shaft, published attribution

states.note: The reported 3.90 m depth belongs to the earlier shaft; it is not a Roman burial-depth datum.

states.label: D9 Roman burial reuse

phase.label: Roman burial, published attribution

states.note: A rectangular burial shaft with a recessed ledge was cut into the side of the earlier Middle Bronze shaft. No entry-60 mouth/grave crosswalk follows.

states.label: N.S.1 reported Roman cistern

phase.label: Roman, assemblage/author attribution

states.note: Rescue-dug toward Khirbet Mefjar on the camp outskirts. No plan was made; no relation to the on-tell grave group is established.

states.label: Trench II/Site O shaft graves

phase.label: Stage XXIV, phase lxxvi

states.note: About eighteen burials in the excavated area, mostly northern. Source-reported shafts with lateral recesses; normally mudbrick closures. Maximum surviving depth 1.25 m below present surface is not the intact ancient surface datum.

states.label: First-century AD grave-type attribution

phase.label: First century AD, typological attribution
phase.dating_basis: Comparison with II cemetery and Qumran grave types; no offerings in these graves

states.note: This interpretive dating draws on the same expedition/publication lineage. Common grave type does not identify a burial community or the Scroll tombs.

states.label: Later pits cutting grave shafts

phase.label: Stage XXV, phase lxxvii; absolute date unknown

states.note: Pits truncate many grave shafts and contain backfilled rubble. Quarry function is Kenyon’s interpretation; their absolute opening date and accessibility beside surviving graves remain unknown.

states.label: Near-north strip skipped by cemetery search

phase.label: Historical search coverage, ancient feature state unknown

states.note: Kenyon II p. 169 reports superficial deposits and a skipped strip just north of the tell. This is missing coverage, not an observed empty ancient landscape.

states.label: Historical irregular spring basin

phase.label: Nineteenth-century descriptions/1856 photograph; construction date unknown

states.note: SWP 24 × 40 ft dimensions are quoted through Dorrell; the original SWP text is not newly inspected. Irregular successor basin is distinct from the modern reservoir.

states.label: Historical curved wall and niche

phase.label: Historical photographic remains; construction date unknown

states.note: Curved wall behind the basin, with niches/stucco and later patching/plundering. Protected photographs are link-only; no wall polygon is traced.

states.label: Late Roman/Byzantine wall attribution

phase.label: Late Roman or Byzantine, scholarly opinion
phase.dating_basis: Architecture/comparanda; no sealed lowest-course deposit cited

states.note: Retains Dorrell’s tentative interpretation without assigning a secure ancient construction year.

states.label: Reservoir enlargement in 1898

phase.label: 1898 documented reservoir work

states.note: Dorrell p. 111 reports extension of the c. 1891–93 mill-pool into the present reservoir in 1898. The modern back wall lies about 1 m east of the old curved spring-house wall.

states.label: Reservoir layout in the January 1908 plan

phase.label: January 1908 recorded layout

states.note: North–south basin curved at the north, with mill southeast. No controlled georeferenced overlay is supplied.
